body:
Thanks for reporting! You have been thorough in your investigation, your conclusion that `ngx-markdown` is a problem here is correct. It is indeed somewhat related to #29835, which was also because of an incompatibility due to ES5 downleveling.

For libraries that have been compiled with `downlevelIteration`, TypeScript does not generate `Array.prototype.slice()` calls (those are supported) but instead inserts a call to `tslib`'s `__spread` helper. We need to add basic support for statically interpreting those calls to resolve this issue. The problem with `tslib` mostly is that it could also be embedded into the file itself, in which case it is harder to identify and insert special behavior for it.

This is also tracked internally in FW-1298

Perfect, thank you very much for the quick response! I was already going crazy trying to find a solution. I suppose then that we simply have to wait. Is there any way to track the FW-1298 ?

Many thanks
@Aw3same I marked this under FW-1298 and any upcoming PR will reference this issue number, so this issue should be closed automatically once a fix gets in :)
@JoostK I tried building my own lib with `downlevelIteration: false` and this error doesn't disappear 🙁

@SebastianPodgajny Maybe there's more reason to use `__spread`, I don't know for sure. Can you share the relevant snippets of code (basically NgModule metadata in the ES5 file) from your library, so we can get an idea of what the issue could be?

It happens on `fesm5 as esm5` step, one thing I found is that if I disable `importHelpers` this step will pass and error will happen on `esm5 as esm5` step so:
enabled `importHelpers` (default ng-packagr)
`fesm2015 as esm2015` ✅ 
`fesm5 as esm5` ❌ 
`esm2015 as esm2015`  ❌ 
`esm5 as esm5`  ❌ 

importHelpers: false
`fesm2015 as esm2015` ✅ 
`fesm5 as esm5` ✅ 
`esm2015 as esm2015`  ✅ 
`esm5 as esm5`  ❌
@Aw3same I can't tell from that screenshot/code sample, is there a (minimal) reproduction available?

issue.body:
The usage of array spread syntax in source code may be downleveled to a
call to TypeScript's `__spread` helper function from `tslib`, depending
on the options `downlevelIteration` and `emitHelpers`. This proves
problematic for ngcc when it is processing ES5 formats, as the static
evaluator won't be able to interpret those calls.

A custom foreign function resolver is not sufficient in this case, as
`tslib` may be emitted into the library code itself. In that case, a
helper function can be resolved to an actual function with body, such
that it won't be considered as foreign function. Instead, a reflection
host can now indicate that the definition of a function corresponds with
a certain TypeScript helper, such that it becomes statically evaluable
in ngtsc.

Resolves #30299
